title: PR calendar 2027 for Philippine brands

slides.title: Why a Calendar Beats *Reacting*
slides.body: Reactive releases almost always arrive late. A calendar means data, photos and spokespeople are ready **before** reporters start looking.

slides.title: Q1 · Jan–Mar
items: Annual results & 2027 targets: release your 2026 milestones
Holy Week (25–26 Mar 2027): newsrooms slow, publish before

slides.title: Q2 · Apr–Jun
items: 12 Jun Independence Day: community and local-pride stories
Mid-year data from your own customers

slides.title: Q3 · Jul–Sep
items: MSME Development Month (July): MSME stories have a news peg
National Heroes Day (30 Aug 2027): frontliners & employee stories
"Ber" months start: plan Christmas campaigns now

slides.title: Q4 · Oct–Dec
items: Bonifacio Day (30 Nov) & Christmas slowdown: publish early

slides.title: The *T-14 to T+3* Rule
slides.body: A working timeline for every moment:
slides.ex: T-14 research & data · T-7 final release + photos · T-3 pitch reporters · Day 0 publish & share · T+3 coverage recap

slides.label: business enterprises in the Philippines (2023)

captions_meta.li_hook:
The brands that show up in the news around big moments prepared their releases weeks before.
Here is a 2027 PR calendar framework for the Philippines.
li_body: With 1,246,373 enterprises in the country (DTI, 2023), competition for attention around peak moments is real. Preparation, not volume, decides who gets covered.
li_points: Q1: annual milestones, Holy Week (newsrooms slow, so publish before), summer and graduation angles.
Q2: Independence Day on 12 June, back-to-school and mid-year customer data.
Q3: MSME Development Month in July, National Heroes Day, and the start of the "ber" months for Christmas planning.
Q4: 11.11 and 12.12, Bonifacio Day and the Christmas slowdown. Publish early.
For every moment: T-14 research, T-7 final release, T-3 pitch, Day 0 publish, T+3 recap.
captions_meta.li_close: Which moment matters most for your brand next year?
